title: AI Medical Coding Platforms With Under-24-Hour Turnaround
summary: Explore 10 AI medical coding platforms and compare their turnaround times, automation capabilities, and published performance results.
body_markdown:
[AI medical coding platforms](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/ai-medical-coding-solutions) promise real-time processing, same-day billing, or coding in seconds. However, these claims don't always represent the time required to complete an entire medical coding workflow.


For health systems, physician groups, and[revenue cycle management (RCM) companies](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/healthcare-revenue-cycle-management-software-companies) , the important question is whether a platform can consistently deliver billing-ready encounters within 24 hours, including the time spent on coding validation, documentation checks, and exceptions.


This article compares ten AI medical coding platforms with under-24-hour turnaround capabilities or relevant speed evidence. It examines their published results, the workflows those results cover, and the limitations buyers should understand before selecting a platform.

## 1. CombineHealth


[CombineHealth](https://www.combinehealth.ai/resources/customer-success-stories/case-study/brault-autonomous-coding) is a **self-learning autonomous medical coding platform designed to help healthcare organizations maintain coding accuracy and fast turnaround across complex clinical workflows.**


CombineHealth analyzes complete patient encounters, assigns diagnosis and procedure codes, determines evaluation and management (E/M) levels, applies[modifiers](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/modifiers-in-medical-billing) , identifies documentation gaps, and handles site-specific coding requirements. Encounters requiring clarification can be routed for review rather than released with unsupported codes.


CombineHealth's main advantage for buyers prioritizing turnaround is its demonstrated performance in live[emergency medicine coding](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/ai-medical-coding-companies-for-emergency-department) .


> CombineHealth's Proven Turnaround Results

> At Brault, an established emergency medicine RCM organization, **CombineHealth maintained a coding turnaround below 12 hours even when incoming chart volumes rose two to three times above normal.**
>
>
> During a separate production event, a hospital released approximately a week's worth of delayed charts in one batch, triggering a fivefold spike in coding volume. CombineHealth absorbed the surge and cleared the backlog without delaying Brault's regular billing cycle.[Read the case study](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/ai-medical-coding-companies-for-emergency-department)


**Additional operational highlights include:**


- **24-hour coding SLA:** CombineHealth can operate under a contractual 24-hour coding SLA, accommodating both routine volume fluctuations and sudden bulk releases of charts, depending on workflow complexity and review requirements.
- **Complex emergency medicine coding:** **The** turnaround results cover workflows involving CPT procedures, ICD-10-CM diagnoses, E/M leveling, modifiers, MIPS, CDI opportunities, and site-specific coding rules.
- **Coding accuracy:** CombineHealth maintained[98.4% accuracy across key coding dimensions](https://www.combinehealth.ai/resources/customer-success-stories/case-study/brault-autonomous-coding) **** in recurring production audits at Brault, including **99.1% for primary ICD, 98.4% for CPT, 98.2% for E/M, and 98.7% for MIPS,** demonstrating that faster turnaround did not compromise[coding accuracy](https://www.combinehealth.ai/resources/customer-success-stories/case-study/brault-autonomous-coding) .

**Best For:** Hospitals, enterprise health systems, and emergency physician groups, seeking accurate autonomous coding with predictable turnaround during fluctuating chart volumes.


## 2. Fathom


Fathom provides autonomous medical coding software for emergency department (ED) professional coding, primary care, and radiology. It assigns E/M levels, diagnosis codes, procedure codes, modifiers, and other required coding details.


Fathom reports that ApolloMD, a nationwide physician group with 1,500 physicians and over 4.5 million annual patient visits, reduced coding turnaround from[days to hours](https://www.fathomhealth.com/ed-pro) .


However, unlike CombineHealth's Brault case study, Fathom has not published exact turnaround times.


For radiology, Fathom publishes a[42-minute average coding turnaround](https://fathomhealth.com/radiology) , with over 97% of encounters going directly to billing. Its[primary care platform](https://www.fathomhealth.com/primary-care-coding-automation) also reports 93% direct-to-bill automation and supports in-person and telehealth encounters.


**Best For:** Emergency physician groups, primary care practices, radiology groups, and RCM organizations seeking high direct-to-bill automation and faster coding turnaround.


## 3. Nym


Nym offers autonomous medical coding software that analyzes clinical documentation, assigns medical codes, and routes successfully coded encounters directly to billing.


Nym specifies a[12-hour turnaround time (TAT) commitment](https://nym.health/autonomous-medical-coding/implementation/) , with the exact measurement defined during technical integration. Achieving this turnaround, along with at least 95% coding accuracy during user acceptance testing, is required before go-live. But Nym hasn’t mentioned specific coding dimensions’ accuracy the way CombineHealth has showcased.


At Geisinger Health System, Nym reduced individual chart coding time from over[20 minutes to less than 2.5 seconds](https://go.nym.health/case-study-automated-medical-coding-across-all-ed-locations) . However, this measures AI processing speed rather than end-to-end turnaround. Nym expects to autonomously code 50-70% of complete records, depending on specialty, with other encounters requiring additional review.


**Best For:** Health systems and physician groups seeking autonomous coding with defined turnaround and accuracy requirements.


## 4. Maverick Medical AI


Maverick Medical AI offers mCoder, an autonomous coding platform primarily focused on radiology and medical imaging workflows. Maverick states that, with a continuous live feed, mCoder can code eligible reports and send them to billing in as little as two seconds.


However, this represents the fastest processing time for an individual eligible report, not the overall turnaround time for a batch of charts. Maverick does not publish a standardized overall coding TAT on its website. Cases involving incomplete documentation, low-confidence predictions, or complex procedures also require additional review.


The platform also reports direct-to-bill automation exceeding 85%, allowing most eligible reports to proceed to billing without human intervention.


**Best For:** Radiology practices, diagnostic imaging centers, and high-volume imaging networks seeking faster coding and direct-to-bill automation.


## 5. XpertDox


XpertDox offers XpertCoding, an autonomous medical coding platform that combines proprietary AI models with payer-specific rules to generate coded claims.


XpertDox reports that its platform codes more than 91% of incoming claims without manual intervention, with a turnaround time (TAT) of under 24 hours.


The company also reports that Lone Star Circle of Care, a federally qualified health center (FQHC), achieved an average claims processing time of under 24 hours, alongside a 94% reduction in manual effort and a 10% improvement in charge capture.


The published coding turnaround applies to autonomously processed claims. Healthcare organizations evaluating XpertDox should also confirm how quickly the remaining claims requiring human review are completed.


**Best For:** Physician groups, federally qualified health centers (FQHCs), and RCM providers seeking faster medical coding with reduced manual intervention.


## 6. Arintra


Arintra offers an autonomous medical coding platform that generates medical codes directly from clinical documentation and integrates with existing electronic health record (EHR) systems. It also supports clinical documentation improvement (CDI), coding audits, and denial management.


In a customer testimonial, Arintra reported an 18-hour coding turnaround time, helping the organization keep provider incentive payments on schedule. The platform also states that it can code most charts within minutes.


The 18-hour turnaround is a customer-reported result and not a publicly stated contractual SLA. Healthcare organizations considering Arintra should confirm if they have an SLA on turnaround times.


**Best For:** Health systems and physician groups seeking faster autonomous coding with integrated CDI and revenue cycle workflows.


## 7. Dolbey AutoClose


Dolbey offers AutoClose, an autonomous coding feature within its Fusion CAC platform designed to process straightforward outpatient encounters without human intervention.


According to Dolbey, AutoClose operates 24/7 and can process eligible charts in seconds and send them directly to billing, helping healthcare organizations reduce coding backlogs and billing delays.


Dolbey does not publicly list fixed numerical turnaround times (TAT) or formal Service Level Agreements (SLAs) on its website.


The company also reports that many organizations using AutoClose process 10,000 or more charts per month without coder intervention, allowing coding teams to focus on more complex encounters.


**Best For:** Hospitals and outpatient coding departments seeking faster turnaround for routine charts while reducing manual coding workloads.


## 8. CorroHealth PULSE


CorroHealth offers PULSE Coding Automation Technology, an AI-powered medical coding platform that automates coding and charge capture for hospitals and health systems. It supports emergency department (ED) facility coding, E/M services, procedures, observation coding, and ICD-10 diagnosis assignment.


In a health-system case study, CorroHealth reported that turnaround time for charts requiring human intervention is 21.3 hours. The same implementation achieved over 90% chart automation, reducing the volume of encounters requiring manual coding.


Unlike speed claims based solely on AI processing, the 21.3-hour result demonstrates turnaround performance for human-reviewed charts.


But this is a customer-specific outcome rather than a contractual turnaround guarantee. Healthcare organizations should confirm whether similar performance can be maintained across their coding workflows and chart volumes.


**Best For:** Hospitals and health systems seeking faster coding turnaround through high automation rates and specialist review for complex encounters.


## 9. MediCodio CODIO


MediCodio offers CODIO AI, an AI-powered medical coding platform that supports autonomous and human-reviewed coding across more than 35 medical specialties. It uses AutoPilot to code complete charts without human intervention and CoPilot to route complex encounters to certified coders for review.


MediCodio reports an average coding turnaround of under 24 hours at enterprise volume, including certified coder review. This measures the time from chart receipt to submitted codes, rather than just AI processing speed.


The company separately reports that CODIO's initial coding pass takes approximately 1.5 minutes per chart, before any human review.


**Best For:** Hospitals, multispecialty physician groups, and RCM companies seeking under-24-hour average coding turnaround with autonomous processing and certified coder oversight.


## 10. Solventum 360 Encompass


Solventum offers the 360 Encompass Autonomous Coding System, an AI-powered platform that identifies eligible encounters, assigns medical codes, and applies coding and validation rules before sending qualified encounters to billing. Cases requiring additional review are routed to human coders.


According to Solventum, its autonomous coding platform achieves a median facility AI engine coding speed of 8.2 seconds. However, this measures AI processing speed rather than the total time required to complete a billing-ready encounter.


Separately, Solventum offers CodeComplete, an outsourced professional coding service. Its official eGuide reports a 48-72-hour coding turnaround, depending on the client's workflow.


For healthcare organizations requiring under-24-hour turnaround, these figures need careful consideration. The autonomous coding system's published speed does not establish an end-to-end TAT, while the outsourced service's reported turnaround exceeds 24 hours. Buyers should confirm whether Solventum can meet their specific coding turnaround requirements.


**Best For:** Large hospitals and health systems seeking autonomous coding with quality controls and optional outsourced coding support.


## How to Evaluate an AI Medical Coding Platform's Turnaround Time


The best[AI medical coding platform](https://www.combinehealth.ai/ai-medical-coding-software) for a healthcare organization is one that can maintain the required turnaround without compromising coding accuracy, documentation quality, or compliance.


Before choosing a vendor, buyers should validate four major aspects of its performance.


### 1. Check Whether the Vendor Offers a Defined Coding SLA


Ask vendors whether they commit to a specific coding turnaround time through a contractual Service Level Agreement (SLA). A claim such as "coding completed within hours" is difficult to evaluate without a defined time window. Look for commitments such as a 24-hour turnaround and clarify whether the SLA covers all eligible charts or only specific encounter types.


### 2. Evaluate Performance During Volume Spikes


Daily chart volumes rarely remain constant. Hospitals may release accumulated backlogs, experience seasonal increases in patient volumes, or send large batches of charts for processing at once. Ask vendors how their platform handles these sudden increases and whether it can maintain its promised turnaround without creating a coding backlog.


Request production examples that demonstrate how the platform handled bulk chart releases and what happened to turnaround times during those periods.


### 3. Check Whether Faster Turnaround Compromises Coding Quality


Faster coding should not come at the expense of accuracy, documentation review, or compliance. Ask vendors how they maintain coding accuracy while meeting their turnaround commitments, particularly for complex encounters that require additional review.


Also examine how the platform routes incomplete or ambiguous charts for human review, how coding decisions are audited, and whether accuracy is monitored across different encounter types.


### 4. Check Exception Handling and Documentation Requirements


Ask vendors how their platform handles charts with missing documentation, conflicting clinical information, or complex coding requirements. Check whether these exceptions are automatically flagged and routed for human review, how additional documentation is requested, and whether such cases affect the overall TAT. A reliable platform should maintain clear exception-handling workflows without allowing unresolved charts to create backlogs or compromise coding accuracy.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### 1. Can AI Medical Coding Platforms Complete Medical Coding Within 24 Hours?


Yes. Some AI medical coding platforms report coding turnaround below 24 hours, including production results, implementation commitments, and customer-specific outcomes. However, buyers should confirm whether those figures cover the complete coding workflow or only automated processing.


### 2. What Is the Difference Between Medical Coding Speed and Turnaround Time?


Medical coding speed measures how quickly an AI system assigns codes. Operational turnaround measures the time required to deliver a completed, billing-ready coded encounter, including applicable validation and review steps.


### 3. Can AI Medical Coding Maintain Fast Turnaround During Volume Spikes?


Some platforms have demonstrated this capability. For example, CombineHealth maintained[turnaround below 12 hours during two-to-three-times fluctuations](https://www.combinehealth.ai/resources/customer-success-stories/case-study/brault-autonomous-coding) in incoming chart volume at Brault. Performance in other deployments depends on the workflow, automation coverage, and exception-handling arrangements.


### 4. Does CombineHealth offer a contractual 24-hour coding SLA?


Yes. CombineHealth can operate under a contractual 24-hour coding SLA covering both routine volume fluctuations and sudden bulk releases of charts, with the exact coverage scoped to workflow complexity and review requirements. In production at Brault, it has held a sub-12-hour coding turnaround even during 2–3× spikes in chart volume, well inside a 24-hour window.


### 5. Does faster turnaround with CombineHealth come at the cost of accuracy?


No. In recurring production audits at Brault, CombineHealth sustained 98.4% accuracy across key coding dimensions — 99.1% primary ICD, 98.4% CPT, 98.2% E/M, and 98.7% MIPS — while holding turnaround under 12 hours. It also integrates CDI directly into coding and flags incomplete or conflicting documentation for review, so speed does not trade off against documentation quality or compliance.


### 6. How does CombineHealth handle a sudden backlog or bulk chart release?


In one production event at Brault, a hospital released roughly a week's worth of delayed charts in a single batch, triggering a fivefold spike in coding volume. CombineHealth absorbed the surge and cleared the backlog without delaying the regular billing cycle. Ask any vendor for a comparable production example of a bulk release, not just an average-day figure.


### 7. Does CombineHealth's turnaround cover the full coding workflow or just AI processing?


It covers the full workflow. CombineHealth's sub-12-hour result at Brault reflects billing-ready encounters across CPT procedures, ICD-10-CM diagnoses, E/M leveling, modifiers, MIPS, CDI opportunities, and site-specific coding rules — not just the seconds an engine spends assigning a code. That distinction matters when a vendor quotes a "seconds per chart" figure that excludes validation, documentation checks, and exceptions.


### 8. How does CombineHealth handle exceptions without delaying turnaround?


CombineHealth codes eligible encounters autonomously and flags charts with missing or conflicting documentation, surfacing them for review with their rationale rather than releasing unsupported codes. Because exceptions are isolated and routed as it codes, unresolved charts don't pile up into a backlog that compromises the overall turnaround on the rest of the volume.
